findings.finding: The gold crown shows its complete opaque golden inside oval across the bottom, occluding the hair. This reads as an empty product-shot crown placed in front of/on the head, not a head entering the crown.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a worn-front source or depth-split the inner/rear ring so actual wearer covers the interior. Parent has stated replacement in progress.

findings.finding: Wide body (internal petite) with backward cap and Bob hair has a large cream background crescent inside the upper-left cap window. The hair does not cover the full aperture.
findings.recommendation: Fit transformed cap window against actual hair/scalp receiver. Bare-only skin backing is insufficient for hair cases; preserve believable hair continuity when filling or reseating.

findings.finding: Round bare head with Viking helmet shows cream background crescents inside both sides of the helmet opening above the scalp. The helmet appears to float above the head.
findings.recommendation: Seat opening lower or revise helmet crown/front geometry so actual scalp occupies aperture. Check side flaps, forehead clearance, and avoid closing gap merely by covering the eyes.
findings.counterexample: Wide Viking122 reviewed native1024; its dark rim touches the scalp without the same cream gaps.

findings.finding: Broad-body crown-height fitting flattens top pom-poms. Wide beanie112 has a low oval pom-pom; Wide party123 has a visibly pancake-like tuft around 2.5 times wider than tall. The attached crown silhouette can legitimately be lower, but the detached pom-pom is visibly distorted. Round variants46/57 show milder version in sheets.
findings.recommendation: Separate the pom-pom region and preserve its local aspect and texture while moving its attachment to the fitted crown.

findings.finding: Black recolored beret and propeller have residual dark red source pixels in the interior/cuff bands. Native58 and59 make them visible; propeller ribs show red tracks.
findings.recommendation: Review color-mask treatment of low-luminance red pixels while preserving intended material highlights. This is a detail/color issue, not equivalent in severity to an empty aperture.

findings.finding: Wide Bob headband is a thin strip with hard clipped ends and little visible wrap/contact depth. The earlier dangling rolled ends are removed, but native113 still reads comparatively flat against the voluminous hair.
findings.recommendation: Preserve subtle front curvature and side-turn/contact shadow while clipping rear ends to wearer. Avoid increasing the band enough to cover eyebrows.
findings.status: Art refinement; no background leak or detached material observed

report.summary: Three high-severity defect classes remain in these captured proofs: hollow crown interior, Wide Bob backward-cap aperture leak, and Round Viking opening gaps. Medium detail issues include flattened pom-poms, dark red color residue, and flat Wide headband depth. New chef front-view source resolves the prior opaque hollow cavity in these six cases.
report.status: Needs targeted fixes and fresh proofs; no blanket approval

report.task: Read-only targeted follow-up evaluation of six affected hats

scope.limitation: This is a bounded six-hat, two-hair, one-skin review. It does not certify all skins, colors, hair styles or accessories, nor later edits.

resolvedOrImproved.result: New front-view crown no longer exposes opaque golden inner oval; band lies against bare head or Bob. Native1,25,60,61 inspected.
New front-view helmet eliminates old dark cavity and side background crescents. Native26 confirms Round bare contact.
Beanie/party ornaments retain volume across reviewed shapes. Native66 and69 confirm Wide pom-poms are no longer pancake-like. No visible artifact requiring change from joins110/80 found.
Cream background hole eliminated, but material seam issue remains; not fully resolved aesthetically.

remainingFindings.finding: Bare-head clipping includes body sprouts and irregular side protrusions. The knit material colors those tips black, creating jagged black flags, hanging patches, or torn-looking ends. Most obvious on Classic10, Lumpy22, Round34; smaller on Petite46, Pear58, Wide70.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Clip to a smooth fitted scalp/temple envelope that excludes sprouts, with the rear ends occluded. Avoid using full body alpha as the only front-band mask.

remainingFindings.finding: Missing-receiver backing eliminates background holes but creates a visible texture/lighting boundary in the aperture: bright diagonal edge on Round28; horizontal join on Wide64. The original silhouette edge remains visible over the added skin patch.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Fit window within genuine receiver coverage if possible. If backing is needed, blend or reconstruct a continuous matching scalp region so no original cutout edge or texture seam remains inside aperture.

remainingFindings.finding: Wide Bob aperture has a bright potato-skin crescent inserted above the hair where the background hole used to be. Gap is closed, but material continuity is inconsistent with the full Bob crown and differs visibly from the other Bob aperture cases.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Use actual fitted hair coverage/material for hair-backed openings, or seat the aperture entirely within the genuine hair receiver.
